tema: Investigates whether recovery from ME/CFS after local physiotherapy of the cervical muscles is associated with improvement of systemic symptoms and autonomic function.
diseno: Observational study in 1226 hospitalized patients over 11 years, non-responders to outpatient care; daily cervical physiotherapy, self-assessed records of ME/CFS and eight symptoms at admission and discharge, and measurement of pupil diameter. Retrospective registration (UMIN000036634).
hallazgos: The recovery rate was 55.5%, with no differences by sex, age or length of hospitalization; recovery of the eight symptoms (36.6-86.9%) was strongly associated with that of ME/CFS (p < 0.001). Recovered patients had more constricted pupils.
conclusion: There is a strong association between recovery from ME/CFS and that of other symptoms, and this recovery could be due in part to improvement of the autonomic nervous system in the cervical muscles.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions are consistent; the PDF conclusions are more cautious and acknowledge that the effect of cervical modulation on ME/CFS remains unclear, given the design without a control group.

tema: Analyses whether SARS-CoV-2 infection reactivates latent human adenovirus (HAdV) in the oral mucosa of ME/CFS patients.
diseno: Case-control study with saliva from 84 ME/CFS patients and 94 healthy controls, with mild/asymptomatic COVID-19 or no infection; anti-HAdV IgG in saliva and plasma, with paired longitudinal analysis before and after COVID-19 (n = 18).
hallazgos: Only in patients was a significantly elevated salivary anti-HAdV IgG response detected after SARS-CoV-2 infection, confirmed in the longitudinal analysis; there was no elevation in plasma.
conclusion: COVID-19 triggered the reactivation of latent HAdV in the oral mucosa of ME/CFS patients, which would indicate an exhausted antiviral response; the authors suggest considering it to identify patients who could benefit from HAdV-targeted therapies.
triangulacion: Keywords and abstract are consistent around latent viral reactivation and the oral mucosa. The discussion text contains only figure legends, funding and conflicts of interest (some authors with income from a private clinic), with no additional conclusions.

tema: German-language review on post-COVID syndrome with fatigue and exercise intolerance meeting ME/CFS criteria.
diseno: Non-systematic review of the literature and of the authors' own work in research and care.
hallazgos: A considerable proportion of post-COVID cases meet ME/CFS criteria, so the number of those affected is expected to double; it covers epidemiology, terminology, pathogenesis, clinical features, diagnosis and symptomatic treatment.
conclusion: Not stated (no conclusions text available).
triangulacion: Keywords (PEM, orthostatic intolerance, long COVID) and opening text are consistent; conclusions are missing and the abstract is truncated before the results.

tema: Explores differences in aortic stiffness, autonomic function and fatigue severity between CFS patients with and without PEM.
diseno: Cross-sectional study with 101 CFS patients (Fukuda criteria), 82 with prolonged PEM and 19 without; CFQ and FIS; aortic systolic pressure (Arteriograph) and autonomic function (Task Force Monitor).
hallazgos: Patients with PEM had higher FIS, lower central systolic pressure and more mental fatigue. Each point of mental fatigue increased the risk of PEM by 34%, each mmHg of aortic pressure reduced it by 5% and each unit of sympathovagal balance increased it by 330%; no difference survived FDR correction.
conclusion: Greater mental fatigue and resting sympathetic activity and lower central systolic pressure could be related to PEM, but the results should be taken with caution and replicated.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent and share caution about the loss of significance after correction for multiple comparisons; the title is more assertive than the data.

tema: Determines the prevalence of ME/CFS and PEM in patients with long COVID.
diseno: Survey of 465 long COVID patients (mostly white women from North America) with a symptom questionnaire, a short ME/CFS questionnaire and a PEM questionnaire.
hallazgos: 58% met an ME/CFS case definition; of those who self-reported ME/CFS, only 71% met criteria, and 40% of those who did not report it did meet them.
conclusion: ME/CFS has a high prevalence among people with persistent COVID-19 symptoms, with over- and underdiagnosis in self-report.
triangulacion: Keywords and abstract are consistent; the conclusions text appears to belong to another article (McManimen and Jason, on comorbidity with fibromyalgia), so it cannot be used for triangulation.

tema: Summarizes the sequelae, viral agents, pathophysiology and treatments of post-viral syndromes of pain, fatigue and sleep disturbances.
diseno: Narrative review with a search in Medline, PubMed and Embase of studies on viruses associated with post-viral syndrome.
hallazgos: Post-viral syndromes include persistent pain, fatigue, musculoskeletal and neuropathic pain, neurocognitive difficulties and sleep disorders; the literature is dominated by small studies and only a small fraction of patients achieve complete recovery.
conclusion: Much of the pathophysiology remains unknown and, given the growing number of COVID-19 survivors with prolonged symptoms, it is urgent to investigate mechanisms and targeted therapies.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent; the PDF expands on the abstract by pointing out the low rate of complete recovery and the possible future value of preventive strategies based on virus-CNS interaction.

tema: Discusses whether chronic fatigue syndrome after bacterial infection, especially post-treatment Lyme disease syndrome, can be explained by a latent infection.
diseno: Narrative review/opinion on latent infection, dormant bacteria and post-infectious chronic fatigue syndrome. No sample stated.
hallazgos: Distinguishes latent infection (asymptomatic and with reactivation) and the asymptomatic carrier from post-infectious CFS, characterized by subjective symptoms without relapses or evidence of viable bacteria.
conclusion: There is no evidence that the symptoms of post-bacterial CFS are due to a latent bacterial infection or to carrying viable bacteria; other causes could be involved, including psychological trauma or still-unknown microorganisms.
triangulacion: Keywords, opening text (with bilingual header) and conclusions are consistent in denying latent infection; the conclusions add the hypothesis of psychological factors and unidentified pathogens, which do not appear in the keywords.

tema: Perspective article reflecting on how PEM is understood, assessed and investigated in daily life and in experimental exercise models.
diseno: Narrative review / perspective; no own sample.
hallazgos: Patients describe PEM with varied terms, with immediate or delayed onset and a duration of days to months; in standardized tests onset is more immediate. There are indications of altered muscle metabolism and autonomic responses on repeated exercise.
conclusion: It is necessary to study the processes of the recovery period after exercise, when PEM reaches its peak.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions are consistent. The discussion adds a cautious nuance: similar deviations appear in other groups and in overtrained athletes, so their diagnostic value requires further study.

tema: Examines the association of PEM with symptom burden and psychological distress in CFS patients according to Fukuda criteria.
diseno: Comparison of patients with high and low PEM within a sample diagnosed with Fukuda criteria; size and methods not stated in the available text.
hallazgos: The study replicates the association between PEM and greater symptom burden and additionally associates PEM with greater psychological distress.
conclusion: Psychological distress could be a consequence of symptom burden; the differences between groups reflect the heterogeneity of the Fukuda criteria, and PEM could identify more affected patients who would benefit from psychological intervention.
triangulacion: The abstract is only the cover page of the preprint; the information comes from the PDF conclusions, consistent with the keywords (symptom burden, psychological distress, mood). The authors qualify the causal direction.

tema: Reviews the definition, pathophysiology, assessment and management of POTS as a heterogeneous and multifactorial disorder.
diseno: Narrative review based on a PubMed search of English-language articles published between 1990 and June 2012.
hallazgos: The pathophysiology includes impaired sympathetic vasoconstriction, excess sympathetic drive, volume dysregulation and deconditioning; many patients have non-orthostatic symptoms and cognitive-behavioural factors that contribute to chronicity. Management combines non-pharmacological measures, drugs and cognitive behavioural therapy.
conclusion: POTS is a chronic condition without a clear pathological substrate, similar to other functional disorders, whose chronicity would depend on central plastic changes in interoceptive processing; behavioural approaches would be more useful than pharmacotherapy.
triangulacion: Keywords and abstract agree on pathophysiological heterogeneity and autonomic dysfunction; the discussion places much more weight on somatic hypervigilance and behavioural factors, a focus not reflected in the keywords.

tema: Editorial commenting on the study by Lewis et al. on POTS as a clinically important subgroup of CFS.
diseno: Editorial / commentary; provides no own data.
hallazgos: Highlights that about 13% (24/179) of CFS patients had POTS and that they differed in fatigue severity, depressive symptoms and daytime hypersomnolence. Proposes validating in other settings, studying differences by sex, different diagnostic criteria and the role of deconditioning.
conclusion: POTS is a clinically important subgroup of CFS and its presence agrees with the evidence that CFS is a disorder of the central nervous system; research on its course and treatment is required.
triangulacion: Keywords, opening text and conclusions are consistent; the conclusion introduces more forcefully the interpretation of CFS as a CNS disorder, supported by external literature rather than by the study commented on.

tema: Determines the prevalence of POTS in CFS/ME patients.
diseno: Observational cohort study: 59 CFS/ME patients (Fukuda criteria) and 52 matched controls; autonomic assessment with continuous heart rate and beat-to-beat blood pressure during 2 min of standing.
hallazgos: Maximum standing heart rate was higher in CFS/ME (106 vs 98 bpm). 27% of patients had POTS versus 9% of controls (p=0.006), and fatigue was associated with the increase in heart rate.
conclusion: POTS is frequent in CFS/ME and clinical evaluation should include the response to standing; studies on its optimal management are needed.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent (conclusions taken from the abstract); they reinforce the high prevalence of POTS and the recommendation to measure the orthostatic response.

tema: Examines a British cohort of POTS patients and compares their symptom burden and functional limitation with CFS patients.
diseno: Cross-sectional study with 136 POTS patients (84 from PoTS UK and 52 from Newcastle clinics) compared with a matched CFS cohort; fatigue, sleepiness, OGS, HADS, HAQ and cognitive failures scales.
hallazgos: The PoTS UK cohort was younger, with fewer men, more employment and longer diagnostic delay; more than 60% had university education. Compared with CFS, fatigue and sleepiness were comparable, but the autonomic burden was greater; there were 21 treatment combinations and up to a third without treatment.
conclusion: POTS patients are mostly young, educated women, with disabling symptoms that affect quality of life, and without consistent treatment.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions (from the abstract) are consistent on symptom burden and disability; the conclusions do not include the comparison with CFS.

tema: Proposes the concept of 'autoimmune autonomic dysfunction syndromes' to group CRPS, fibromyalgia, CFS, breast implant symptoms and post-COVID syndrome.
diseno: Review with conceptual proposal; no systematic methodology stated.
hallazgos: The syndromes share pain without evident tissue damage and autonomic alterations; after a trigger (trauma, infection, silicone), autoantibodies against receptors of the autonomic nervous system are produced that would amplify pain and other symptoms.
conclusion: The unifying term would guide research in animal models and clinical studies to improve diagnosis and direct treatments.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent; the conclusions are very emphatic ('revolutionary', 'undoubtedly') for a hypothesis that is not yet validated.

tema: Systematic scoping review that maps the causal factors of ME/CFS investigated in primary studies.
diseno: Systematic scoping review in eight databases; 1161 primary studies (1979-2019) classified by two reviewers into 9 categories and 71 subcategories of factors, based on title/abstract.
hallazgos: No causal factor dominates; mean of 2.73 factors per study. The most studied: immunological (297), psychological (243), infections (198) and neuroendocrine (198). Case-control studies predominate (894) and more than half include 100 or fewer participants.
conclusion: Causal research is diverse but mostly hypothesis-generating; larger and better-designed studies are needed, especially prospective cohorts.
triangulacion: The three sources agree on the heterogeneity and weakness of the designs. The PDF conclusions add a recent decline in research on infections and interest in post-COVID-19 fatigue, not highlighted in the abstract.

tema: Sets out, in a hypothesis-driven review, the molecular mechanisms of muscle fatigue in long COVID and other viral infections (HHV-6, Powassan, EBV, HIV) and its similarity to ME/CFS.
diseno: Narrative literature review on viruses, adaptive immunity, demyelination and mitochondrial metabolism. No sample stated.
hallazgos: Proposes that infection of CD4+ T lymphocytes or antigen-presenting cells induces inflammatory cytokines, recruitment of T lymphocytes to the CNS, central and peripheral demyelination and altered neuromuscular transmission; CD8+ muscle infiltration and mitochondrial energy deficit are also discussed.
conclusion: The review offers a mechanistic hypothesis of chronic muscle fatigue from prolonged viral infection, noting that it is not known whether SARS-CoV-2 directly infects T lymphocytes.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions are consistent around post-viral muscle fatigue; the conclusions are more detailed and make explicit uncertainties (T lymphocyte infection by SARS-CoV-2) that the abstract does not mention.

tema: Evaluates the diagnostic potential of serum activin B as an ME/CFS biomarker.
diseno: Case-control study with 134 ME/CFS patients and 54 healthy controls; validated plasma activin B ELISA and visual analogue scale (VAS) of symptoms.
hallazgos: Activin B did not differ significantly between patients and controls (p = 0.6511), nor by sex or age; it showed a non-significant tendency to decrease with higher VAS scores (r = -0.2004; p = 0.5085).
conclusion: The results do not agree with previous work and do not support the clinical usefulness of activin B as an ME/CFS biomarker.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent with a negative result; the PDF conclusions mention the tendency with the VAS as something requiring more data, without reinterpreting it as positive.

tema: Explores the composition of the gut and oral microbiota and the faecal metabolomic profile in CFS/ME versus controls.
diseno: Case-control study with 105 participants: 35 patients (Fukuda criteria), 35 cohabiting relatives and 35 healthy controls; 16S rRNA sequencing of stool and saliva and UHPLC-MS metabolomics in a subgroup.
hallazgos: In patients' stool there was a reduction in Lachnospiraceae (Anaerostipes) and an increase in Bacteroides and Phascolarctobacterium; in saliva, an increase in Rothia dentocariosa. The faecal metabolome showed more glutamic and argininosuccinic acid and less alpha-tocopherol.
conclusion: There are dysbiosis signatures in CFS/ME, compatible with the autoimmune hypothesis and with altered glutamatergic signalling in the microbiota-gut-brain axis; whether they are cause or consequence remains to be clarified.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent. The conclusions go beyond the abstract in supporting the autoimmune hypothesis and pointing to similar changes in relatives, suggesting environmental or genetic factors.

tema: Estimates the prevalence of Aspergillus-derived mycotoxins (ochratoxin A, aflatoxin, gliotoxin) in the urine of ME/CFS patients chronically exposed to mould.
diseno: Prevalence study with 236 ME/CFS patients from South Florida with a history of chronic mould exposure (water-damaged buildings); urinary analysis of mycotoxins and their distributions.
hallazgos: Evidence of exposure was found in 92.4% of patients, with ochratoxin A the most prevalent; the mycotoxin distributions showed right skew.
conclusion: The findings are preliminary; it is unclear whether these patients form a subgroup or whether mycotoxins contribute to disease onset or progression, and controlled studies with larger samples are required.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions are consistent; the conclusions are more cautious than the prevalence headline, stressing the absence of a control group and causal uncertainty.

tema: Examines progressive brain changes associated with CFS using longitudinal MRI.
diseno: Longitudinal study with 1.5 T MRI in 15 patients and 10 controls scanned twice 6 years apart; grey and white matter volumes, T1/T2 intensities, voxel-based morphometry and symptom scores.
hallazgos: Decreased white matter volume in the left inferior fronto-occipital fasciculus (IFOF) in CFS, with no change in controls, with lower grey matter volume in adjacent and contralateral regions; these volumes correlated with symptoms.
conclusion: CFS is associated with white matter deficits in the IFOF that continue to deteriorate after onset.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent on white matter atrophy and the IFOF; the conclusions (from the discussion) are more cautious and acknowledge loss to follow-up and non-validated symptom scales.

tema: Studies the time course of acetylcholine-induced vasodilation in the skin microcirculation of CFS patients.
diseno: Case-control study with 30 CFS patients and 30 healthy controls matched for age and sex; single transdermal ACh dose (iontophoresis) and measurement of cutaneous blood flow.
hallazgos: There were no differences in peak flow, but recovery was slower in patients: time to 75% of peak 13.7 ± 11.3 versus 8.9 ± 3.7 min (p = 0.03) and to 50%, 24.5 ± 18.8 versus 15.1 ± 8.9 min (p = 0.03).
conclusion: The prolonged ACh vasodilation suggests an alteration of cholinergic pathways, perhaps in the vascular endothelium, which could be related to the hypotension, orthostatic intolerance and POTS associated with CFS.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and discussion are consistent; the discussion is more cautious in limiting the finding to ACh as an endothelium-dependent vasodilator and noting that its meaning for vascular integrity remains to be determined.

tema: Analyses cytokines in extracellular vesicles and plasma proteomic data to distinguish ME/CFS cases from controls and relate them to clinical features.
diseno: Case-control study with frozen plasma samples from a cohort with prior cytokine and proteomic data; multiplex cytokine assay in EVs, multi-omic statistical analyses with clinical data and machine learning classifiers; sample size not stated.
hallazgos: Cases had EVs of larger size and concentration, and significantly higher EV IL2. Higher CSF2 and TNFα correlated with more physical and fatigue symptoms, and SERPINA5 with better SF-36 general health. XGBoost with 20 proteins reached 86.1% accuracy (AUROC 0.947) and Random Forest with 7 proteins 79.1% (AUROC 0.891).
conclusion: The findings add to the objective biomolecular differences in ME/CFS and implicate alterations of the immune response and haemostasis; they must be confirmed in a larger sample before possible diagnostic use.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent on EVs, cytokines and proteomics; the PDF conclusions highlight the value of clinical data and are more cautious about diagnostic usefulness, whereas the keywords do not include machine learning.

tema: Quantifies the duration and severity of PEM symptoms after a two-day CPET in ME/CFS.
diseno: Study with 80 ME/CFS patients (Canadian Criteria) and 64 sedentary controls; nine-symptom Symptom Severity Scale over 10 days; pharmacokinetic models.
hallazgos: Recovery time was 12.7 days in ME/CFS versus 2.1 in controls (range 1-64 versus 1-10); fewer than 10% took more than three weeks and one did not recover in a year. Prior severity did not matter and the models showed a very prolonged decay.
conclusion: Patients take about two weeks to recover versus two days in controls; the data improve informed consent and, according to the authors, support caution regarding graded exercise therapy.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent. The PDF conclusions go beyond the abstract in stating that graded exercise therapy would almost certainly cause harm, an inference based on the models.

tema: Reviews the biological abnormalities shared between acute COVID-19 and ME/CFS, centred on redox imbalance, and their possible relevance for long COVID.
diseno: Narrative literature review on oxidative stress, systemic inflammation, neuroinflammation, ATP production and hypometabolic state. No sample stated.
hallazgos: Both acute COVID-19 and ME/CFS present redox imbalance, systemic inflammation and neuroinflammation, lower ATP generation and a hypometabolic state, with bidirectional relationships between these processes; these phenomena have not yet been well studied in long COVID.
conclusion: The same abnormalities are likely to appear in long COVID; studying the connection between redox, inflammation and energy metabolism could lead to new diagnoses and therapies.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent; the conclusions add other possible mechanisms (cerebral hypoperfusion due to autonomic dysfunction, autoantibodies) and qualify that some long COVID symptoms may be due to organ damage.

tema: Examines autonomic nervous system activity at rest and after acute exercise in ME/CFS.
diseno: Case-control study with 20 ME/CFS patients and 20 healthy people; cardiac, respiratory and electrodermal responses at rest and after an acute exercise session.
hallazgos: At rest, time-domain parameters were normal, whereas frequency-domain ones indicated possibly lower (para)sympathetic activation. After exercise, reduced parasympathetic reactivation was observed during recovery.
conclusion: There is lower autonomic modulation and parasympathetic reactivation after exercise in ME/CFS; since slow heart rate recovery is associated with a worse prognosis in other conditions, studies on how to improve it safely, with sufficient recovery periods, are warranted.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent; the PDF conclusions add the recommendation of long recovery periods and warn that the prognostic implication in ME/CFS remains to be tested.
